item: A queued substitution for the throw-in taker is not applied at that throw-in (brief: "Applied by subsTick at the next stoppage")
detail:
In /home/user/Fifa/src/sim/rules/subs.ts, takerBusy() (lines 172-178) defers an entry when the restart taker's act is anything other than NONE or SET_PIECE. For a throw-in, RUL-11/RUL-02 do not use SET_PIECE as the waiting action. They put the thrower in ActionKind.THROW_IN from the first tick of the phase: restart.ts beginTakerAction (line 378), and isWaitingAct (restart.ts:208) counts NONE, SET_PIECE and THROW_IN as waiting. The waiting sub-states are ThrowState.APPROACH, HOLD and CHARGE in throwin.ts:163. So the thrower counts as 'mid-kick' for the whole THROW_IN phase, even though throwin.ts handlerEnd (around line 988) is built to be interrupted: it drops the ball back on the line.

I reproduced this with a throwaway probe against the real step() pipeline. The ball was pushed over the touchline, and on the first THROW_IN tick requestSub(team, restart.taker, benchOutfielder) returned 1 with the taker's act already THROW_IN.
- CPU v CPU (humans=0): the sub was not applied during the throw-in. It was applied only at the next stoppage, a CORNER at tick 592, about 560 ticks later.
- With humans (humans=2): the taker was still in THROW_IN at tick ~420, the last tick the probe logged, and the sub had not been applied when the run ended at tick 1534.

In the real game this hits a user who pauses at a throw-in, or answers the quick-sub prompt, to replace the thrower (often a tired full-back). The sub is silently held until a later stoppage.

This is also untested. The only taker test (rul-10-subs.test.ts:452) covers a FREE_KICK taker in KICK versus SET_PIECE. Suggested fix: only treat the taker as busy once he has committed. For a throw-in that means act === THROW_IN with actA === ThrowState.WINDUP (3) or actDone === 1. Treat APPROACH (0), HOLD (1) and CHARGE (2) as waiting, like SET_PIECE. Then add a scenario test that queues a sub for the throw-in taker and expects it to apply within the THROW_IN phase.
